cards.title: AI Ads: Use Context, Not Volume
cards.summary: Most AI ad generation fails because it produces high-volume generic 'slop' instead of ads built on proven angles and specific customer avatars.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to deploy AI tools for paid social ad production and are tempted to bulk-generate ads quickly.
steps: Treat AI as an accelerant layered on top of an existing creative strategy, not as a standalone strategy. The source argues brands winning with AI are the ones who already have strategy and use AI to speed execution.

Before generating anything, feed the tool deep context: your brand URL, a defined list of competitors, and your product catalog. A tool that scrapes your site can build a brand book (do's, don'ts, must-haves) that improves every future output.
Research recurring competitor angles as inspiration, then test original concepts for the store. Public ad-library presence does not prove an ad is profitable.
Expect losers even with good context. The presenter describes roughly 50% usable output as an excellent result when context is strong—not 100%.
Keep producing your own human creative alongside AI output; AI is explicitly framed as not a total replacement for creative production.
caveats: Source is a sponsored-feeling walkthrough of one specific AI tool; verify current tool features and pricing before committing.
The ~50% usable-output figure is the presenter's stated personal expectation, not a measured benchmark.
Accessing exact incremental revenue/ROAS per ad requires connecting your ad account, not just the public ad library.
cards.source_name: The Best AI Ad Creative Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Avatar + Template = Ad Concept (Creative as Targeting)
cards.summary: Shift from building ads for manual audiences to building ad concepts from an avatar plus a template, letting Meta's algorithm use the creative messaging to find the audience.
cards.use_when: You are structuring new ad concepts and deciding how to organize targeting, ad sets, and messaging intent in your prospecting campaign.
steps: Define the specific buyer avatar first (e.g., hair-loss buyer vs. weight-loss buyer). The presenters' 'new way' is: avatars create audiences.
Pair that avatar with a creative template (format/angle) to produce a single ad concept. Example formats cited: 'GLP-1's New Bestie,' iPhone Notes, '60 ingredients, one gummy.'
Let the messaging in the creative do the audience targeting on Meta's algorithm rather than relying primarily on manual backend audience selection.
Group ads strictly by avatar inside a campaign. Do not mix, for example, hair ads and weight-loss ads in the same ad set, because that muddies the messaging intent the algorithm reads.
When generating with AI, include the avatar and the borrowed template explicitly so the output stays on-message.
caveats: This is the presenter's stated 'new way' opinion for 2026 Meta advertising; results depend on account, offer, and creative quality.
Template/angle inspiration drawn from competitor ads should be adapted, not copied verbatim.

cards.title: Pack-Based Modular Creative Testing Structure
cards.summary: Launch each new round of creatives as a 'pack' ad set grouped by avatar, sized 4–8 ads, inside the prospecting campaign.
cards.use_when: You are setting up prospecting campaign structure and deciding how to organize and isolate new creative rounds.
steps: Keep a simple two-campaign structure: a prospecting campaign and a retention campaign. Focus testing inside prospecting.
Every time you launch a new round of creative, create a new 'pack' ad set (e.g., broad pack one, broad pack two). New ads = new pack; new concept = new pack.
Group packs by avatar: keep different avatars' ads in separate ad sets even when they sit in the same campaign.
Size a pack between 2 and 10 creatives, with 4–8 ads as the stated sweet spot—enough angles to test without diluting spend across too many angles.
Pause, keep, or modify packs over time; the structure is meant to be modular and evolving as you run more rounds.
caveats: Pack counts scale with account size (one pack today could be many later); no fixed universal number.
Grouping by avatar assumes you have clearly distinct avatars; overlapping avatars may warrant different grouping.

cards.title: Seven-Day Minimum Budget Constraint to Force Creative Testing
cards.summary: Set an ad-set minimum spend equal to 1x target CPA for 7 days to force the algorithm to test new creatives, then remove it to let winners scale.
cards.use_when: You are launching new creative packs and need to guarantee they get a fair chance at spend rather than being starved by the algorithm.
steps: Go to the ad set (your 'pack') budget section and find ad set spending limits.
Set the daily minimum dollar value to 1x your cost-per-acquisition (CPA) target. If target CPA is $50, enter $50.
If that figure equals too large a share of your budget, cap it at 20% of the daily budget maximum.
Apply this as a 7-day minimum so new ads are tested at your target CPA; if they perform, they spend above the minimum; if not, they fade and scale down.
After 7 days, remove the minimum constraint and let the pack run freely so the best ads scale naturally.
caveats: The 7-day and 1x-CPA figures are the source's recommended heuristics, not a proven universal benchmark.
The 20% cap is the presenter's suggested safeguard for smaller budgets; verify current Ads Manager budget-limit interface before setting.
cards.source_name: The Best AI Ad Creative Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Iteration Engine: Scale Winners from Incremental Revenue Data
cards.summary: Find top ads by incremental revenue and incremental ROAS, then produce meaningful variations—not word-level tweaks—of those winning concepts.
cards.use_when: You have winning ads in the account and want to systematically expand them into new iterations for continued prospecting.
steps: In the main prospecting campaign, open all ads and go to the column set, selecting the attribution comparison for incremental attribution.
Sort ads by incremental revenue and incremental ROAS to surface ads that drove revenue that wouldn't have occurred without the ad.
Take the top ads and produce variations—either by re-generating with an AI tool using the winning ad as input, or by manually tweaking them.
Make iterations a 'decent swing': in the presenter's framing, an iteration today would have qualified as a wholly new ad in old-school Facebook—not just changing one word in the headline.
Feed each new iteration round into the pack-based testing structure as a new pack.
caveats: Incremental attribution requires proper account setup and interpretation; verify current column-set options in Ads Manager.
Incremental ROAS is more reliable than relevance scores or impressions from the public ad library.
cards.source_name: The Best AI Ad Creative Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: What 'Good' AI Ad Output Looks Like
cards.summary: Judge AI ad output by whether it maps to a named, proven angle or format—not by raw volume produced.
cards.use_when: You are reviewing a batch of AI-generated static or video ad concepts and deciding which to run and which to discard.
steps: Check each output for an explicit concept/angle label and an 'inspired by' reference to a proven competitor or your own winning ad.
Flag outputs you personally dislike (the presenter skipped a generic 'lifestyle in kitchen' concept) and either discard them or regenerate variants.
Reformat as needed: a 4x5 concept can be regenerated to 9x16 with one click in the cited tool.
Prefer concepts tied to demonstrated winners—e.g., formats proven in the brand's own ad account or widely used across the niche (GLP-1 'New Bestie,' iPhone Notes, '60 ingredients, one gummy').
Use a starter prompt library ('expert library' prompts like 'winning ad iteration' or 'top of funnel creative testing') to standardize high-quality inputs across the team.
caveats: Specific formats named are examples from the source's niche (supplements), not universal winners; adapt angle to your category.
Tool prompt libraries and format-conversion buttons are tool-specific; verify they exist in your current tool.
